title: Pathfinder: Constructing Cycle-accurate Taint Graphs for Analyzing Information Flow Traces
problem: Hardware information flow tracking generates massive violation traces requiring manual analysis of hundreds/thousands of signals to identify root causes.
motivation: Automated root cause identification in IFT traces dramatically reduces verification burden for detecting security vulnerabilities.
method: Pathfinder constructs taint graphs (maps showing how information flows through a circuit at each clock cycle) by combining two analysis techniques: taint tracking (which follows how data moves) and self-composition (which compares system states to spot differences). The system creates these graphs at cycle-accurate precision, tracking information flow at each step. From violation traces (records of unwanted information flows), it automatically extracts only the relevant signals, eliminating the need to manually analyze hundreds or thousands of signals.
key_novelty: It automatically generates cycle-accurate maps of information flow from violation records, eliminating the manual analysis work that would otherwise require searching through hundreds of signals.
contributions: Theoretical foundation unifying taint tracking and self-composition
Automated taint graph generation from simulators or formal model checkers
Signal relevance extraction reducing manual analysis 1.6-769.9x
Case studies demonstrating effectiveness on constant-time, Trojans, Spectre violations

metrics.speedup: 1.6-769.9x reduction in signals requiring manual analysis
metrics.other: effective on constant-time, Trojans, Spectre violations

limitations: Requires HDL source; applicability limited to designs with available RTL descriptions.
primary_theme: automated IFT root cause analysis via taint graphs
